answer.rationale: Hard constraint is do not raise delivery risk: the line is at 94% with no buffer and the primary contract lapses in 14 days without auto-renewal, so a full cutover or a deferral would put downstream assembly at risk. Incumbent already refused a mid-cycle reopen, but expiry is the actual leverage point; c4 says benchmarking at renewal moved price and terms, and the low-cost quote is a concrete BATNA if c2’s quick-onboard/accurate-invoice record holds. Prefer a short, guarded renegotiation that keeps incumbent integration (c1) and seeks the 18% cut without an irreversible primary switch or a multi-year lock-in. Verifying c2 and c4 before treating either path as settled; c5-style month-to-month deferral does not apply here.
